adoption_score.limit: A heuristic blend with hand-picked weights.
adoption_score.name: Adoption Score

cache_savings.how: Cache reads billed at 10% instead of 100%, minus the 25% premium for cache writes, at list prices.
cache_savings.limit: Assumes you would otherwise have sent the same tokens uncached.
cache_savings.name: Cache savings

clean_turns.how: Turns that finished with no tool error, no interruption, and no correction from your next prompt, divided by all turns.
clean_turns.limit: A correction is detected from wording at the start of your next prompt, so it can miss some.
clean_turns.name: Clean first-pass turns

cold_start.how: Cost of each session's first call as a share of all session cost.
cold_start.name: Cold-start tax

cost.how: Token usage priced at the PRICING table in the script.
cost.limit: List prices; $0 real marginal cost on a subscription.
cost.name: Estimated cost

cost_100_loc.how: Estimated cost divided by lines Claude wrote, times 100.
cost_100_loc.limit: Lines of code are additions only.
cost_100_loc.name: Cost per 100 lines

cost_spikes.how: Days costing 2x or more your typical day in the window.
cost_spikes.limit: Needs five or more active days.
cost_spikes.name: Cost spikes

cost_verified.how: Estimated cost of sessions that edited and then ran a check, divided by their count.
cost_verified.name: Cost per verified session

first_edit.how: Seconds from a session's first log entry to Claude's first edit, median over sessions that edited.
first_edit.limit: Edits made through shell commands are not seen.
first_edit.name: Time to first edit

first_run.how: For each session and kind of check (test, build, lint), whether the first run passed.
first_run.limit: Pass/fail comes from the command's error flag.
first_run.name: First-run pass rate

flow_score.how: 50% clean-turn rate + 30% failure-recovery rate + 20% (1 - stuck share); needs 5+ turns.
flow_score.limit: A heuristic blend; the trend matters more than the number.
flow_score.name: Flow score

friction.how: Failed tool results per 100 edits, and interruptions per 100 prompts.
friction.limit: A failed command is often a normal step.
friction.name: Errors and interruptions

hotspots.how: Files edited 5+ times that were edited 3+ times in one session or on 3+ days.
hotspots.name: Rework hotspots

model_mix.how: Each model's share of estimated cost, by session.
model_mix.limit: A session's primary model is the one that cost the most.
model_mix.name: Model mix

perms.how: The decision and source recorded with each tool call, when the logs include it.
perms.name: Permission decisions

quality_score.how: 40% verified + 20% tests alongside + 20% low re-edits + 20% first-run pass (when checks ran); needs 3+ edited sessions.
quality_score.limit: A heuristic blend; the trend matters more than the number.
quality_score.name: Quality score

recovery.how: Of the times a tool failed, the share where the same tool later succeeded in that session.
recovery.limit: A different fix that does not retry the same tool counts as unrecovered.
recovery.name: Failure recovery

reedit.how: Edits to a file already edited earlier in the same session, divided by all edits.
reedit.limit: Normal step-by-step work also re-edits files.
reedit.name: Re-edit share

safety.how: Counts of risky commands (force-push, hard reset, recursive delete, pipe-to-shell, skipped hooks) and touches of secret-like files.
safety.limit: Pattern matching on command text; only category counts are stored.
safety.name: Safety signals

session_len.how: Last entry minus first entry in a session (median, 90th percentile).
session_len.name: Session length

stuck.how: Failure episodes where the same tool failed three or more times in a row.
stuck.limit: Three failures is a convention, not a law.
stuck.name: Stuck loops

tests_alongside.how: Sessions that edited a test file, divided by sessions where Claude edited.
tests_alongside.limit: Detected from file names such as test_*, *.spec.*, tests/.
tests_alongside.name: Tests alongside code

thinking.limit: Only present when the logs include it.
thinking.name: Thinking time

tool_time.how: Time between each tool call and its result, grouped by tool or command.
tool_time.limit: Excludes the model's own thinking and generation time.
tool_time.name: Where tool time goes

top_tier_nocode.how: Share of top-tier-model cost spent in sessions where Claude made no edits.
top_tier_nocode.limit: Some thinking-heavy sessions legitimately need a top-tier model.
top_tier_nocode.name: Top-tier model on no-edit sessions

turn_time.how: Time from your prompt to Claude finishing its answer (stop reason end_turn); median and 90th percentile.
turn_time.limit: Includes any time spent waiting for you to approve an action.
turn_time.name: Turn time

verified.how: Sessions where a test, build or lint command ran after Claude's last edit, divided by sessions where Claude edited.
verified.limit: Running a check is not the same as the check passing.
verified.name: Verified after last edit

capabilities.detail: 5 responses with token usage (0 duplicate log lines dropped)
capabilities.label: Tokens and cost

capabilities.detail: 3 turns timed from your prompt to Claude finishing
capabilities.label: Turn timing

capabilities.detail: 2 of 2 tool results matched to their call
capabilities.label: Tool timing

capabilities.detail: Pass/fail comes from the error flag; exit-code text seen on 1 failed commands
capabilities.label: Command outcomes

capabilities.detail: None in these logs, so accept/reject rates are not shown
capabilities.label: Permission decisions

capabilities.detail: 1 of 2 sessions have an AI title
capabilities.label: Session titles

limits: Edits Claude makes through shell commands (sed, python scripts) are not counted as edits or lines of code.
Turn and tool times include any time spent waiting for you to approve an action.
The logs do not show which of Claude's output you kept, so there is no true acceptance rate unless permission decisions appear.
A session is not a task: a long session can hold several tasks, and one task can span sessions.
Cost is an estimate at public list prices; on a subscription plan your real marginal cost is $0.
